## From LCL track files to a locus experiment

This guide uses the package's subset of the actual **AL6_bc2162_19093** and
**AL8_bc2170_19151** LCL files at **ALAS1** and **PRDX1**. It shows the input
fields, coordinate conversions and R objects at each step. These are small
processed track files, with matching complete records and regenerated tabix
indexes. The subset is capped at 100 full-span reads per sample per locus;
the available totals are 18 reads at ALAS1 and 16 at PRDX1.

All analysis runs in R. The package expects processed tracks rather than BAM
or FASTQ files. See **Select Fiber-seq loci: ALAS1 with and without clustering**
for the full set of clustered and unclustered panels.

| Function | Accepted input | Output / next step |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `example_data()` | New or empty writable directory | A list containing `samples`, `regions` and `directory` |
| `make_sample_sheet()` | `data.frame`, `DataFrame`, or a headered TSV path | Sample `DataFrame` for validation and analysis |
| `prepare_regions()` | `GRanges`, coordinate table/string, headerless BED, or GTF/GFF3 | Named `GRanges` for validation and analysis |
| `extract_canonical_tss()` | GTF/GFF3 with a specified canonical attribute | Optional alternative source of region `GRanges` |
| `validate_inputs()` | Sample sheet plus region `GRanges` | Invisible `TRUE`, or an informative error |
| `analyze_loci()` | Samples, regions and explicit clustering choice | Named `SimpleList` of `RangedSummarizedExperiment` objects |
| `locus_profile()` | One locus experiment | `DataFrame` of pooled or cluster-wise fractions |
| `plot_locus()` | One locus experiment, panel type and view | `ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap`, ggplot or patchwork composition |
| `cluster_colors()` | Cluster labels or factor levels | Original cluster colors, shared by all plots |
| `write_locus_results()` | One experiment or the whole results list | RDS, TSV and PDF files in a new or empty directory |

## 1. Copy the example into a writable directory

```{r copy-example}
library(selectFiberseqLociWorkflow)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(GenomicRanges)

example <- example_data()
names(example)
list.files(example$directory)
```

`example$directory` is a temporary writable copy. To keep the inputs, supply a
persistent destination, for example `example_data("my-LCL-example")`.
`samples.tsv` and `regions.tsv` describe the files under `tracks/`.
`provenance.json` records original source paths and selected read IDs;
`SHA256SUMS` records checksums. The subset-generation script is installed at
`system.file("scripts", "build_example.py", package = "selectFiberseqLociWorkflow")`.
The examples below use only this copied dataset and installed package files.

## 2. Sample sheet: one row per sample

Read the actual TSV as an ordinary R table to inspect its fields:

```{r raw-sample-sheet}
sample_table <- read.delim(file.path(example$directory, "samples.tsv"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(sample_table[, c("sample_name", "sample_label", "m6a")])
knitr::kable(sample_table[1, c("m6a_format", "nucleosome_format",
    "tf_format", "fire_format")], row.names = FALSE)
```

| Column(s) | Required? | Meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `sample_name` | Yes | Unique read namespace and sample key; use letters, digits, `_`, `.` or `-` |
| `sample_label` | No | Display label; defaults to `sample_name` |
| `m6a`, `m6a_format` | Yes | Path/template and explicit modification-track format |
| `nucleosome`, `nucleosome_format` | No | Path/template and format for a supplied nucleosome track |
| `tf`, `tf_format` | No | Path/template and format for supplied TF footprints |
| `fire`, `fire_format` | No | Path/template and format for a supplied FIRE track |

`make_sample_sheet()` normalizes this table to an `S4Vectors::DataFrame`.
For an in-memory table, `base_dir` resolves relative paths. For a TSV filename,
paths are resolved relative to the TSV's directory. Optional tracks can be
omitted or have blank paths; a supplied path needs its matching format.

```{r normalized-sample-sheet}
samples <- make_sample_sheet(sample_table, base_dir = example$directory)
from_tsv <- make_sample_sheet(file.path(example$directory, "samples.tsv"))
stopifnot(identical(samples, from_tsv))
class(samples)
samples[, c("sample_name", "sample_label", "m6a_format", "tf_format")]

# Save a new sample sheet with resolved paths and read it back.
saved_sheet <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
make_sample_sheet(sample_table, base_dir = example$directory,
    output = saved_sheet)
stopifnot(identical(samples, make_sample_sheet(saved_sheet)))
```

Only `{sample_name}` and `{chr}` are supported placeholders. The actual LCL
sheet uses sample-specific folders and `{chr}`. A single genome-wide file per
sample can instead be supplied without `{chr}`. Each supplied track must be
**bgzip-compressed, sorted and tabix-indexed**, with its `.tbi` beside it.

This is the same LCL sheet expressed using both placeholders:

```{r sample-template}
template_table <- sample_table
for (track in c("m6a", "nucleosome", "tf", "fire")) {
    template_table[[track]] <- paste0("tracks/{sample_name}/", track,
        ".{chr}.bed.gz")
}
template_samples <- make_sample_sheet(template_table,
    base_dir = example$directory)
```

## 3. Regions: declare the coordinate convention

The actual `regions.tsv` is a **headered table**. Its `start` and `end` use BED
coordinates: zero-based start, end excluded. Its `tss` is one-based. Read the
table first, then declare `coordinate_system = "bed"`:

```{r region-table}
region_table <- read.delim(file.path(example$directory, "regions.tsv"))
knitr::kable(region_table[, c("region_id", "chr", "start", "end",
    "strand", "tss")])
regions <- prepare_regions(region_table, coordinate_system = "bed")
regions
alas1 <- regions["ALAS1"]
```

The ALAS1 interval `[52197159, 52199159)` becomes
`chr3:52197160-52199159` in R: 2,000 bases, one-based inclusive. PRDX1 is on the
minus strand, but its genomic start is still less than its end. Coordinates
are not reversed for minus-strand loci.

| Input to `prepare_regions()` | Coordinate convention | Details |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `GRanges` | One-based inclusive | Preserves sequence information; names identify regions |
| `data.frame` / `DataFrame` | Explicit `"bed"` or `"one_based"` | Required `chr`, `start`, `end`; optional `region_id`, `strand`, `tss` |
| Headerless BED path | Zero-based, half-open | First three fields are contig/start/end; field 4 is region ID and field 6 is strand |
| `"chr3:52197160-52199159"` | One-based inclusive | Plain coordinate string; no TSS or gene metadata inferred |
| `annotation = "file.gtf"` or `"file.gff3"` | One-based annotation coordinates | Transcript features define TSSs; see annotation examples below |
| Custom single-base TSS BED | Zero-based, half-open | Optional `bed_annotation = "gencode_custom"`; name field is `geneID;annotation;geneName` |

Do not pass a headered `regions.tsv` directly as a BED filename. `flank_bp`
expands annotation-derived TSSs or custom TSS BEDs; ordinary coordinate inputs
already specify the full analysis interval.

The following representations all describe the same ALAS1 interval:

```{r equivalent-region-inputs}
one_based <- region_table[region_table$region_id == "ALAS1", ]
one_based$start <- one_based$start + 1L
from_one_based <- prepare_regions(one_based, coordinate_system = "one_based")
from_string <- prepare_regions("chr3:52197160-52199159")
from_granges <- prepare_regions(alas1)

bed_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".bed")
write.table(data.frame(chr = "chr3", start = 52197159, end = 52199159,
    name = "ALAS1", score = 0, strand = "+"), bed_file,
    sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
from_bed <- prepare_regions(bed_file)

for (r in list(from_one_based, from_string, from_granges, from_bed)) {
    stopifnot(as.character(seqnames(r)) == "chr3",
        start(r) == start(alas1), end(r) == end(alas1))
}

# Exported region tables also use BED start/end and one-based TSS.
saved_regions <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
prepare_regions(regions, output = saved_regions)
round_trip <- prepare_regions(read.delim(saved_regions),
    coordinate_system = "bed")
stopifnot(identical(start(round_trip), start(regions)),
    identical(end(round_trip), end(regions)),
    identical(mcols(round_trip)$tss, mcols(regions)$tss))
```

Contig names must match exactly between regions and track indexes, including
case. No chromosome prefix conversion or genome-assembly conversion is done.

## 4. Inspect a real record from each LCL track

The format is declared in the sample sheet, not guessed from the filename or
from whether the user ran fibertools or FiberHMM. These are the supported
formats; the LCL subset uses the four marked in the final column.

| Track | Format string | Fields | Present in this LCL subset? |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| m6A | `bed12_fibertools` | BED12 blocks, including terminal sentinel blocks | Yes |
| Nucleosome | `bed12_fibertools` | BED12 blocks, including terminal sentinel blocks | Yes |
| Nucleosome | `bed13_fiberhmm` | BED12 plus per-block scores; no sentinel removal | No; supported alternative |
| TF | `bed15_fiberhmm_tf` | BED12 plus block scores and left/right edge-score vectors | Yes |
| TF | `bed6_per_sample` | `chr`, `start`, `end`, `RID`, `score`, `strand`; one prefiltered interval per row | No; supported alternative |
| FIRE | `bed11_fire` | Per-read interval with FIRE score and a trailing tag | Yes |

Here are the first actual AL6 records on chr3. The short helper below is only
for displaying a few lines in this vignette; it is not a package function.
Comma-separated block vectors are truncated in the display, not in the files.

```{r inspect-track-records}
track_names <- c("m6a", "nucleosome", "tf", "fire")
track_files <- vapply(track_names, function(track)
    sub("{chr}", "chr3", samples[[track]][1], fixed = TRUE), character(1))
stopifnot(all(file.exists(track_files)),
    all(file.exists(paste0(track_files, ".tbi"))))

read_first_record <- function(path) {
    con <- gzfile(path, open = "rt")
    on.exit(close(con))
    strsplit(readLines(con, n = 1L), "\t", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
}
raw_records <- lapply(track_files, read_first_record)
bed12_fields <- c("chrom", "chromStart", "chromEnd", "RID", "score", "strand",
    "thickStart", "thickEnd", "itemRgb", "blockCount", "blockSizes",
    "blockStarts")
field_names <- list(m6a = bed12_fields, nucleosome = bed12_fields,
    tf = c(bed12_fields, "blockScores", "leftEdgeScores", "rightEdgeScores"),
    fire = c(bed12_fields[1:9], "fire_score", "tag"))
record_preview <- do.call(rbind, lapply(track_names, function(track) {
    values <- raw_records[[track]]
    data.frame(track = track, field = seq_along(values),
        name = field_names[[track]],
        value = ifelse(nchar(values) > 65L,
            paste0(substr(values, 1L, 65L), "..."), values))
}))
knitr::kable(record_preview, row.names = FALSE)
```

For BED12, fields 2 and 3 are the alignment's BED bounds; `blockStarts` are
offsets from field 2. Block vectors have `blockCount` entries. Fibertools'
first and last blocks are sentinels and are removed before calls are used.
m6A interior blocks must each be one base wide. Reads with no interior m6A
calls in the selected region still contribute to the denominator if they
span the region.

For the actual TF BED15, field 13 contains scores for individual blocks.
`min_tf_score = 50` filters those scores, not field 5. Retained TF width
classes are [10,30), [40,60) and [60,80) bp. BED6 TF intervals are expected to
be score-filtered already; the same width classes apply. The default retained
nucleosome widths are 130 through 160 bp inclusive.

FIRE records are per-read intervals, joined by their original RID. The trailing
tag may contain legacy haplotype labels in these source files; the package
does not use that field to phase or split reads. Allele-specific RDS inputs
are not needed. Optional track RIDs must match the m6A RIDs within each sample;
records for reads excluded by full-span filtering do not enter the result.

### Follow one m6A call into R coordinates

Use the first actual AL6 record and one of its interior calls inside ALAS1:

```{r one-real-call}
raw_m6a <- raw_records$m6a
block_offsets <- as.integer(strsplit(raw_m6a[12], ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
block_sizes <- as.integer(strsplit(raw_m6a[11], ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
interior <- seq_along(block_offsets)
interior <- interior[-c(1L, length(interior))]
call_positions <- as.integer(raw_m6a[2]) + block_offsets[interior] + 1L
inside <- which(call_positions >= start(alas1) & call_positions <= end(alas1))
chosen <- interior[inside[1L]]
chosen_position <- as.integer(raw_m6a[2]) + block_offsets[chosen] + 1L
knitr::kable(data.frame(original_RID = raw_m6a[4],
    alignment_start_BED = as.integer(raw_m6a[2]),
    block_offset = block_offsets[chosen], block_width = block_sizes[chosen],
    position_in_R = chosen_position))
```

The formula is `position_in_R = chromStart + blockStart + 1`. We will locate
this exact call in the sparse assay below.

## 5. Validate and analyze

`validate_inputs()` checks file/index availability, the required m6A contigs,
and declared record structure in sampled records. Parsing during analysis
performs further checks on records in the requested region. It does not
certify every record in a whole-genome file.

```{r validation}
validate_inputs(samples, regions)
validate_inputs(template_samples, regions)

# An expected error: a supported TF format cannot be used for m6A.
bad_samples <- samples
bad_samples$m6a_format <- "bed15_fiberhmm_tf"
tryCatch(validate_inputs(bad_samples, alas1), error = conditionMessage)
```

Choose clustering explicitly. This run makes both LCL loci without clustering:

```{r analyze-lcl}
results <- analyze_loci(samples, regions, clustering = FALSE)
names(results)
x <- results[["ALAS1"]]
x
metadata(x)$qc
data.frame(locus = names(results),
    bases = vapply(results, nrow, integer(1)),
    reads = vapply(results, ncol, integer(1)))
```

Only the longest overlapping alignment of a read is considered, and it must
span the entire region. All retained reads, including those with zero m6A
calls, remain in the matrix. The standard read order is sample-sheet order,
alignment start, then RID.

## 6. How `GRanges`, the assay and `colData` agree

`results` is a named `SimpleList`. Each element is a
`RangedSummarizedExperiment` with **genomic bases in rows and reads in columns**.
`assay(x, "m6a")` is a sparse binary matrix. A zero means no observed m6A call
at that genomic position, not an experimentally measured unmethylated adenine.

| Component | Structure | Alignment with the assay |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `rowRanges(x)` | Single-base `GRanges`, one-based inclusive | One range and matching row name per assay row |
| `colData(x)` | `DataFrame` of read metadata | One row and matching RID per assay column |
| `colData(x)$read_range` | `GRanges` of full alignments | One alignment per assay column; agrees with `chr`, `start`, `end`, `strand` |
| `colData(x)$footprints` | `GRangesList` | One list element per read, with `RID`, `track` and `class` metadata on its intervals |
| `metadata(x)` | List | Original region, sample sheet, QC, parameters and optional clustering provenance |

The column ID is `sample_name::original_RID`, so the same original RID in two
samples does not collide. All in-memory alignment and footprint coordinates
are one-based inclusive. Stored footprints can extend beyond the locus if an
original call overlaps its boundary.

```{r aligned-containers}
class(assay(x, "m6a"))
rowRanges(x)[1:3]
colData(x)[1:3, c("RID", "original_RID", "sample_name", "start", "end")]
colData(x)$read_range[1:3]
colData(x)$footprints[1]

rid <- paste(samples$sample_name[1], raw_m6a[4], sep = "::")
row_id <- paste("chr3", chosen_position, sep = ":")
assay(x, "m6a")[row_id, rid]
stopifnot(assay(x, "m6a")[row_id, rid] == 1,
    identical(names(rowRanges(x)), rownames(x)),
    identical(rownames(colData(x)), colnames(x)),
    identical(colData(x)$RID, colnames(x)),
    all(start(colData(x)$read_range) == colData(x)$start),
    all(end(colData(x)$read_range) == colData(x)$end))
```

### Subset using the standard Bioconductor interface

```{r subset-experiment}
small <- x[1:20, c(3, 1)]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(small), rownames(colData(small))),
    identical(colData(small)$read_range, colData(x)$read_range[c(3, 1)]),
    identical(colData(small)$footprints, colData(x)$footprints[c(3, 1)]))
small
```

Subsetting keeps ranges and read metadata attached to the correct assay
columns. Row subsetting does not clip the stored footprint intervals, and
`metadata` keeps the original run's QC and clustering graph as provenance.
For the current subset's fractions, use `locus_profile(small)`; it recomputes
the denominator from the currently selected read columns.

## 7. Profiles, plots and optional clustering

`locus_profile()` returns `pos` (one-based), `group`, `cov` (number of retained
reads), `met` (reads with a call), `frac = met / cov`, and the smoothed fields
`smooth_cov` and `smooth_frac`. The `base` field is labeled `A` for m6A; the
package does not fetch a reference sequence. Only positions observed in at
least one retained read are reported, except that an all-zero locus returns
all positions. A locus with no full-span reads has `NA` fractions.

```{r profile-and-plot}
profile <- locus_profile(x)
head(profile)
stopifnot(all(profile$cov == ncol(x)),
    isTRUE(all.equal(profile$frac, profile$met / ncol(x))))
plot_locus(x, "profile")
```

Use `plot_locus(x, "heatmap")` for a `ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap` object and draw
it with `ComplexHeatmap::draw()`. `"profile"` returns a ggplot;
`"footprints"` returns a patchwork stack of the profile, m6A reads and
overlaid FIRE/nucleosome/TF tracks. Both read panels place sample annotations
farthest left, then cluster annotations. Colors, TSS markers and themes follow
the original plotting tutorial. The analysis vignette executes all three panel types in both modes.

Clustering controls are user-settable arguments. The defaults are
**`window_size = 0`, `k_neighbors = 10`, `resolution = 1`**. Zero bin size means
individual observed sites; a positive integer sets clustering-bin width in bp.
The bin feature is each read's mean call across observed sites in that bin.
The assay remains single-base. Neighbors are capped at `ncol(x) - 1`;
resolution is a nonnegative Leiden parameter. `smoothing_bp = 10` separately
controls the profile smoothing width.

```{r cluster-with-chosen-settings}
# These explicit values are the current defaults.
clustered <- analyze_loci(samples, alas1, clustering = TRUE,
    window_size = 0, k_neighbors = 10, resolution = 1, seed = 1)[["ALAS1"]]
colData(clustered)[1:3, c("RID", "cluster")]
head(locus_profile(clustered, by_cluster = TRUE))
stopifnot(identical(assay(x), assay(clustered)),
    identical(locus_profile(x), locus_profile(clustered)))

# Change the controls for a new fit; no package code needs editing.
binned <- analyze_loci(samples, alas1, clustering = TRUE,
    window_size = 50, k_neighbors = 5, resolution = 0.5)[["ALAS1"]]
metadata(binned)$parameters[c("window_size", "k_neighbors", "resolution")]
```

Use the public palette helper to carry the original cluster colors into your
own figures. Factor input retains all levels, including unobserved clusters.

```{r cluster-palette}
cluster_colors(colData(clustered)$cluster)
cluster_colors(c("cluster3", "cluster1"))
```

`plot_locus(clustered, "profile", clustered = TRUE)` uses a separate denominator
for each existing cluster. The `clustered` plot argument does not fit a model.
With fewer than three reads or two occupied features, clustering is skipped;
inspect `metadata(x)$clustering_status` before requesting cluster views of
other datasets. Unclustered results are independent of clustering parameters.

## 8. Omitted, empty and missing optional tracks

An m6A-only sheet is valid. It produces the same m6A assay and profile, with
empty footprint ranges. Omitting optional tracks produces no empty-footprint
warning:

```{r m6a-only}
minimal_samples <- make_sample_sheet(samples[,
    c("sample_name", "sample_label", "m6a", "m6a_format")])
minimal <- analyze_loci(minimal_samples, alas1, clustering = FALSE)[["ALAS1"]]
stopifnot(identical(assay(minimal), assay(x)),
    all(lengths(colData(minimal)$footprints) == 0L))
metadata(minimal)$supplied_tracks
```

A **supplied** nucleosome or TF track that has no retained footprints in the
region raises the warning:

> no footprints called in the selected region

Analysis continues, and `metadata(x)$empty_footprint_tracks` records the
affected track types with no retained calls across the supplied samples.
This can also happen after size or score filtering.
A supplied nonexistent file or missing `.tbi` is instead an input error.

## 9. GTF/GFF3 annotations and optional canonical selection

The LCL examples above use their actual coordinate table. The following
annotation files are **synthetic plant fixtures**, included to illustrate
additional accepted input structures without misrepresenting them as LCL
GENCODE annotations.

GTF needs transcript feature rows with `gene_id`, `transcript_id` and strand;
`gene_name` is optional. GFF3 needs transcript/mRNA rows with unique `ID` and
gene `Parent` relationships. Gene rows with `ID` and `Name` supply gene names.
Exon-only files are insufficient. Coordinates and contig names are preserved.

```{r annotation-structures}
gff <- system.file("extdata", "plant", "annotation.gff3",
    package = "selectFiberseqLociWorkflow")
gtf <- system.file("extdata", "plant", "annotation.gtf",
    package = "selectFiberseqLociWorkflow")
cat(paste(readLines(gff), collapse = "\n"), "\n")
cat(readLines(gtf)[1], "\n")
```

Ordinary extraction does not require canonical tags. A plus-strand TSS is
the transcript start; a minus-strand TSS is its end. Distinct TSSs are retained;
transcripts sharing a gene/TSS/strand are recorded together in `transcript_ids`.
The default `flank_bp = 1000` produces `[TSS - 1000, TSS + 999]` in one-based
inclusive coordinates; `flank_bp = 0` returns one-base TSSs. Windows extending
before position 1 are rejected.

```{r ordinary-annotations}
plant_regions <- prepare_regions(annotation = gff)
plant_regions
prepare_regions(annotation = gff, genes = "PlantGene2", flank_bp = 0)
prepare_regions(annotation = gff, transcripts = "AT5G00010.2", flank_bp = 500)
prepare_regions(annotation = gtf, genes = "AT5G00010")
```

`extract_canonical_tss()` is an optional stricter helper. Its default is
`attribute = "tag", value = "Ensembl_canonical"`, suitable for tagged GTFs.
A different attribute/value pair can be specified for GFF3. Unlike ordinary
region preparation, its default `flank_bp = 0` returns just the TSS; supply
`flank_bp = 1000` to analyze a promoter window.

```{r canonical-annotations}
extract_canonical_tss(gtf, genes = "AT5G00010", flank_bp = 1000)
extract_canonical_tss(gff, genes = "AT5G00010",
    attribute = "canonical", value = "true", flank_bp = 1000)

# Expected error: this GFF3 gene has no canonical tag. Ordinary extraction
# above succeeds because it does not require that tag.
tryCatch(extract_canonical_tss(gff, genes = "PlantGene2",
    attribute = "canonical", value = "true"), error = conditionMessage)
```

Each selected gene must have exactly one matching canonical transcript;
missing or ambiguous selections are reported as errors. Plant regions can be
analyzed with the same `analyze_loci()` call when the supplied processed tracks
use these exact contigs and supported formats. Do not pair the plant fixture
coordinates with the human LCL tracks.

## 10. Save results and load them again

`write_locus_results()` accepts either one experiment or the entire named list.
This example saves both loci without clustering; the main analysis vignette
also saves a clustered run with both plot views.

```{r export-input-guide}
output <- tempfile("lcl-results-")
write_locus_results(results, output)
list.files(file.path(output, "ALAS1"), recursive = TRUE)
restored <- readRDS(file.path(output, "ALAS1", "locus.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(assay(restored), assay(x)),
    identical(rowRanges(restored), rowRanges(x)),
    identical(colData(restored), colData(x)))
```

| File or directory within each locus | Contents |
|:--|:--|
| `locus.rds` | Complete experiment, including range columns and parameters |
| `m6a_matrix.rds` | Sparse assay only |
| `reads.tsv` | Flattened read metadata; `read_range` and `footprints` remain in the RDS |
| `qc.tsv` | Per-sample overlapping and full-span read counts |
| `region.tsv` | Headered BED-coordinate table with one-based TSS |
| `unclustered/` | `m6a_heatmap.pdf`, `aggregate_m6a_profile.pdf`, `footprint_tracks.pdf`, `accessibility_profile.tsv`, `read_order.tsv`, `manifest.tsv` |
| `clustered/` | Additional views after successful clustering; also `assignments.tsv` and `edges.tsv` |

When optional tracks are omitted, `footprint_tracks.pdf` is omitted and the
manifest explains why. With no full-span reads, the experiment still has the
region's rows but zero columns; the manifest reports empty panels. Locus
directory names come from region IDs, with unsafe filename characters replaced
by underscores; colliding names are rejected.

The complete `locus.rds` is the file to reload for plotting and Bioconductor
interoperability. Use a persistent output directory instead of `tempfile()`
to retain results after the R session ends.
